title: bbox_knowledge broad smart-mode queries overflow the token budget and spill to a file
wanted_capability: Output bounding (or a compact/titles-only default) for bbox_knowledge so a broad smart-mode query does not exceed the token budget. A multi-term smart query returned ~81k chars / 1400+ lines twice this session, forcing a spill-to-file and a re-query. A `limit` row-count exists but smart-mode recall-broadening still emits unbounded total bytes; a byte cap or titles-first compact mode (opt into bodies) would keep interactive dedupe checks cheap.
missing_primitive: byte-cap / titles-only compact mode on bbox_knowledge smart queries
fallback_used: Re-queried with mode=substring + a tight phrase + small limit, then grepped the spilled tool-result file
evidence: bbox_knowledge query='rtk grep ripgrep rg fd shell command rewrite quirk' -> 81632 chars
resolution_note: Brick 0 (commit f084a65 on branch feat/knowledge-locate-coherence): bbox_knowledge's broad path now renders system memories as compact signposts (system_memory::format_for_signpost — header + tags + one-line preview + a bbox_knowledge(query="sm-…") retrieval breadcrumb) instead of dumping full ~40KB bodies. Full body still returns on the exact sm-* id short-circuit (exact_system_memory_response). Empty-query worst case ~13KB vs the ~81KB overflow. Knowledge entries (120-byte excerpts) and packets (one-line rows) were already bounded. Pending merge to main. Broader unification (index system memories/packets as first-class doc types) tracked in design/corpus/agentic-corpus/locate-information-coherence.md.
